- Previous white diamond at (7, 49) changed to G(12) - now DARK GRAY
- Purple square stayed at (32, 47) - didn't move

Now the purple diamond at (16, 57) is WHITE. The purple square is at (32, 47). The trail connects them.

1. There are 2 squares: orange at (12, 27), purple at (32, 47)
2. There are 4 diamonds (2 orange, 2 purple). Only one can be white at a time.
3. Clicking a diamond toggles it G↔W (and the other same-color diamond also toggles)
4. Clicking light blue regions or the orange diamond outline moves the purple square
5. The orange square never moves
Current state:
- Purple diamond at (16, 57) is WHITE
- Orange diamond at (7, 49) is DARK GRAY
- Purple square at (32, 47)
- Orange square at (12, 27)
What if the goal is to get BOTH squares to be adjacent to their white diamonds simultaneously? Currently only one diamond can be white at a time.
Wait, let me reconsider. There are 2 orange diamonds and 2 purple diamonds. When I click one orange diamond, it toggles and the OTHER orange diamond also toggles. Same for purple.
So there's always exactly 1 white orange diamond and 1 white purple diamond? No, currently:
- Orange diamond at (7, 49): G (dark gray)
- Orange diamond at (19, 8): G (dark gray)
Both orange diamonds are G! And:
- Purple diamond at (16, 57): W (white)
- Purple diamond at (49, 40): G (dark gray)
So currently only the purple diamond at (16, 57) is white. The orange diamonds are both G.
Wait, that doesn't match my earlier understanding. Let me re-check. When I clicked the orange diamond at (7, 49) to make it W, the purple diamond at (16, 57) became G. Then when I clicked the purple diamond at (16, 57) to make it W, the orange diamond at (7, 49) became G.
So it seems like there's a global toggle: clicking any diamond makes it W and the PREVIOUSLY white diamond becomes G. There's only ONE white diamond at a time, regardless of color.
Hmm, but that seems odd. Let me look at the initial state more carefully. From the very first frame:
- Orange diamond at (7, 49): G
- Purple diamond at (46, 54): G (this was the target)
- Orange diamond at (19, 8): G
- Purple diamond at (49, 40): G
All diamonds were G initially! Then after my first clicks, some became W.
Actually, looking at the initial state from the first turn, I see:
- G(12) at (7, 49) with O center
- G(12) at (19, 8) with O center  
- G(12) at (46, 54) with p center
- G(12) at (49, 40) with p center
All 4 diamonds were G initially. The white diamonds appeared as a result of my clicks.
OK so the mechanic is:
1. Click a G diamond → it becomes W (and creates a white diamond at that location)
2. Click another diamond → the previous W becomes G, the new one becomes W
3. Only one diamond can be W at a time
4. Clicking light blue or orange outline moves the purple square toward the click
The purple square moves along the trail toward the white diamond. The trail connects the square to the white diamond.
So the goal might be: position the purple square at the white diamond's location. When the square reaches the diamond, the level completes.
Currently the purple square is at (32, 47) and the white diamond is at (16, 57). I need to move the square to (16, 57).
But clicking light blue regions moves the square toward the click, not necessarily to the white diamond. The square seems to move along a path constrained by the black background.
Let me try clicking the light blue region that's closest to the white diamond at (16, 57). The light blue regions are:
- S(164) at (22, 25)
- S(138) at (29, 55)
- S(280) at (32, 1)
The closest to (16, 57) is S(138) at (29, 55). But clicking there moved the square away from the target before.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider. The purple square moves when I click light blue regions. The movement is toward the click location, following the trail. The trail goes from the square to the white diamond. So the square moves along the trail path.
If the white diamond is at (16, 57) and the square is at (32, 47), the trail connects them. When I click something, the square moves along the trail toward the white diamond.
So maybe I should just click the light blue region closest to the white diamond, and the square will move along the trail toward it.
Let me try clicking near the white diamond at (16, 57). The closest light blue region is S(138) at (29, 55). Let me click somewhere on it.
Actually, I realize I should look at the trail more carefully. The trail is the white path connecting the square to the white diamond. If I click something, the square moves along this trail.
